reason: Both sources state each of 8 claims in their own words; single-source details were removed after independent QA.
story: On 21 September 1921, workers at BASF's Oppau nitrogen fertilizer plant in Germany broke up a caked, hardened stockpile of ammonium sulfate nitrate with explosives, as they had done before. Hundreds of tons of the fertilizer exploded. More than five hundred people were killed and nearly two thousand more wounded, and the blast destroyed much of the town around the factory. Shortly before, a change to how the fertilizer was made had left it more explosive than anyone foresaw.
angle: Workers used explosives to loosen a fertilizer pile everyone treated as safe, and a recent change in how it was made had turned it into a bomb.
